title: My-Cap Sampler Set - Fill Your Own Coffee Pods - Includes Cap, Lid, Foil Seals, Capsule Holder & Funnel - Complete Solution to Make Your Own Capsules for Nespresso VertuoLine Brewers
reviews: So I bought Nespresso Vertuo which I have found is amazing as I prefer longer coffee's rather than the standard espresso from the Nespresso Classic. All was great until I found out I was moving to Singapore and realised they don't sell the Vertuo line machines or pods there.. I looked around for solutions and read all the reviews on the stainless steel pods and other contraptions. I had a great feeling about the my-cap solution. I ordered the My-Cap Sampler and also the additional 3 pack, I was a bit dubious on how it would go based on my attempts using different reusable pods for the Nespresso Classic. The My-Cap Vertuo solution is amazing.. I've even worked out how to make it fool proof with a little testing. I use freshly ground beans with a Breville grinder (BCG820). After a number of attempts of comparing the ground coffee consistency with that of Nespresso I've managed to get a pretty close grind size, the next hurdle was working out how much coffee to put in. My first attempts were following the manual, using the scoop and tampering down the coffee with the bottom of the scoop. The issue is consistency on volume and tamping pressure, as these are not the same every time my results were more hit than miss but I still got a fair share of horrible noises and red flashing lights from the machine. My solution to give 100% accuracy is using the pod holder and placing this directly under the the grinder. The Breville grinder I have is digital and allows me to accurately select a grind size and grind time to 0.2 sec. So I grind the exact amount into the pod, give it a shake, I tamp it down with a tamper bigger than the top of the pod so the coffee is right to the top and push it down slightly with the silicon cap, dust off any additional grains and I get 100% results. *I don't use the filter paper and have had no issues with grains in the coffee. From my testing it looks like Nespresso add something to their coffee to stop it clumping together. I'm not sure what it is or if I actually want to know, in a recent coffee class in Vietnam the roaster told me they added butter to their beans to prevent the grains sticking, I expect Nespresso do something similar. If I compare my ground coffee to a Nespresso coffee after the coffee has been made, the Nespresso one is still wet and loose, mine is compacted and all the moisture has been drawn out. I would recommend this product to anyone wanting to use it with a digital grinder where you can deliver the perfect amount of coffee every time. You may need to alter the settings slightly for different beans but it will only be 1 or 2 notches. For the coffee beans I have at the moment, my settings are: 150ml Pod = Grind size 25, Grind time 6.0 seconds 230ml Pod = Grind size 25, Grind time 7.4 seconds

So to start off you maybe a bit confused why this product includes both the foils and the silicone disk and filters, basically there are 2 ways to brew and it’s kind of up to you to figure out what works for you, either the foils or the filter/silicone disk way. After testing this, here is my verdict. You don’t need the Filter/silicone disk as this method leaves more mess (inside the machine, no coffee grounds in the cup) it is a longer, more involved option. You want to use the aluminum foils! This is a much easier method since all you need is to fill up the pod with your coffee of choice and seal it with the foil, it works the same way as original, leaves no mess or coffee grounds in your cup and overall the better option since you can make a lot of them and just use them as you wish. The only downside is the foils after reusing them leave glue residue which shortens the life span you can use the pod. The reviews that say foils break and what not are either written by people with defective machine/foils or who simply don’t know how to use their hands. Overall don’t buy this product, instead go and buy my-cup 100q foils as it is cheaper and you will come to the same conclusion regardless.

This is a refill kit for the new version of Verturo Nespresso pods, the ones with the round bottom. I do not know if it works with the other version of Nespresso pods. If you drink a lot of coffee these are a real money saver. The regular pods cost around $1.50 each and you generate a huge amount of waste with the pods. Yes, they are aluminum and you can send them back for recycling, which you should, but what a pain. It's a bit fussy and time consuming to open and clean out the original pods, but once you have a supply of them you can use them over and over, in all the different sizes. It comes with a holder to hold the pod while filling, and a tamper to press the grounds into the pod. Once filled you simply cover the pod with the foil caps and use it like a regular pod. There is no problem with leakage as long as you make sure to seal the foil tightly all around. Also, we had some problems with the machine not working with some of the refilled pods, but the issue was that when we put on the foil top and crimped it around the edge we had covered some of the bar code which is under the rim of the pod. This code tells the machine what size pod you have inserted, and it won't work if it can't read the code, so make sure the bar code is not obscured when you install the new foil cover. Once you have made the coffee and ejected the pod you can peel of the foil and reuse the pod again. There is no difference in taste or functionality beween the refill and the original pod. Very happy to have found these 'refill kits' , they save both money and help keep the pods out of the trash. Again, the Nespresso pods can be sent back for recycling, but why not just reuse the ones you have?

If you want to save money on your Nespresso pods this is the way! Super easy to use and make your own pods. I bought a craft knife to cut the foil off the original pods and it’s been seamlessly easy! Followed the instructions card and it was done in less than a min. Used for my coffee and same great taste.

Bought for my Nespresso Vertuo. I use these with preground espresso coffee, and the taste is good, IMO. The little cup holder helps when filling the little containers. The lids are easy to clean. I found that I like the silicon lids best, and do not use the liners. I thought the price was high for what you get, but then the Nespresso pods are $1.10-$1.20 each, so these are way cheaper to use as they are refillable.

The foils work great and what I'll use moving forward. It was hit or miss with the hard plastic cap, the machine kept giving an error. As soon as I put the silicone cap on it worked fine. Because of the thickness of the silicone, it seemed a bit more difficult to get the fill level right on the capsule. Now for the tip...One thing I found that isn't mentioned is that the green funnel also makes for a handy tool to seal the foil lid. Just put the capsule in the black holder, the foil sits right on top and fits perfectly within the "outer" ring of the black holder, then press down with the green funnel and twist back and forth a bit while pushing down. UPDATE: I found that while this works, a quick press around the edge with the brush handle gets a much better seal - so my revised process is a quick press and turn of the green part keeps the foil in place and then a quick press with the brush handle to finish. Doing it this way, the process of filling a capsule only took about 30 seconds from grinding to popping it in the machine. Being able to use paper filters is also nice to filter out cafestol (elevates cholesterol) if that's a concern for heavy coffee drinkers.

This is so easy to use! I read all kinds of reviews and recommendations looking for a reusable Nespresso Vertuoline cup/device, and My-Cap products were always on the lists. So, I got the My-Cap Sampler. All three tops work great! I use the hard plastic one the least because you can't store it. The silicone top comes with a lid, and the foil tops don't need a cover as they don't have holes. I wasn't really sure what the green part was for at first. It isn't mentioned in any of the included instructions. I use it to seal the foil tops around the edge. It says to use the end of the brush or something to seal the foil on the flat part at the top. The green part works great to do that, and it's faster and more accurate. The barcode still shows on the capsules so it works just like a Nespresso capsule. I highly recommend getting the My-Cap Sampler! You get to try all the different types of lids without breaking the bank.

I am only commenting on the foil reseal part of this system. I owned this product for over a year before trying, now I would not go back to the factory pods. At first I ordered this to see if I could save some money, but after using the system for a couple weeks, I have a whole different take on using it. Now, it's for the infinite variety of coffees I can make. Over the recent holidays I ground my own beans from a couple of various commercial outfits and found the quality fo brew equal or exceeding the factory pods and now I was the one who decided what ratio of specialty brew to make. You can also vary the level of intensity and caffeine you will consume. I was a whole pot kinda guy but now just do two or maybe three cups of very high quality brew. My standard large pod mix is 1/2 pod standard dark roast coffee from C*stco and 1/2 expresso grind that I can do or any commercial espresso brand. For the smaller pods, I go with 100% espresso. A couple tips for recycling: 1. Trim the Mylar factory seals while stabilizing them in the enclosed holder to make the process a little safer using a good sharp exacta knife (the smoother the cut, the better the sticky caps work) 2. Have enough recycled pods to last a week, that way on Sunday you can make up enough for the whole week. 3. After peeling off the foil caps, use a small table spoon to scoop out the used coffee (the drier the better) while standing over your trash receptacle as this can get messy. 4. Use the included brush to remove the few remaining grounds. At this point if you are not doing step #5, then I wipe the lids where the foil seals with a clean damp cloth to ensure the foil seals adhere tightly to keep the coffee fresh by the time it is used. This is also a good time to push out any dents with the back of your fingernail or smooth spoon as they accumulate dents as they are ejected from the brew area. 5, Every two three reuses, I run the pods through by dishwasher on the upper silverware tray just to completely remove any coffee oils that have accumulated. They bounce around a little, but the upper shelf for silverware in my LG helps keep them in place. Enjoy and anyone that understands the bar code processes that vary from the various factory flavors, please share the info or a link. Thanks!
